status_as_of_cutoff: site work-construction: Millard County approved C-2 CUP application #Z-2025-035 on 2025-07-01 for a data center and electrical generating facility at approximately 4500 E & Hwy 50, Delta; Utah GOEO reported on 2026-04-09 that the Creekstone Gigasite began construction in late 2025; Creekstone's current project page and 2026-07-23 company release say construction is underway and firm gas transportation supports the first behind-the-meter generation block. A separate Creekstone solar CUP #Z-2026-043 was noticed for July/August 2026 local process, but final August 4 minutes/approval were not located. No energization, commissioning, certificate-of-occupancy, or live-service record was located.
evidence_grade: B: official county minutes confirm the core data-center/electrical-generation CUP approval and official state economic-development records confirm the construction claim; current company records support construction and initial gas-capacity details. Final building permits, solar CUP outcome, energization, commissioning, and live-service evidence remain unverified.

actions.result_status: Planning Commission minutes show a public hearing and unanimous favorable recommendation to the BOCC on C-2 CUP application #Z-2025-035 for a data center and electrical generating facility at approximately 4500 E & Hwy 50, Delta; the application described 26 buildings.
actions.access_caveat: Official county minutes; recommendation only, not BOCC final approval.

actions.result_status: BOCC minutes show unanimous approval of C-2 CUP application #Z-2025-035 for a data center and electrical generating facility at approximately 4500 E & Hwy 50, Delta, with proposed conditions. The applicant was Fibernet Mercury Delta, LLC; Buford Ray Conley was present and Fibernet Delta said it agreed to the CUP conditions.
actions.access_caveat: Official county minutes; building permit, certificate of occupancy, and energization records were not located.
actions.evidence_note: Official local-government final CUP approval for the data-center/generation use.

actions.government_body: Utah Governor’s Office of Economic Opportunity
actions.result_status: GOEO awarded Creekstone Energy a post-performance rural tax reduction tied to $17,082,408,000 planned investment and 106 jobs; GOEO says the Creekstone Gigasite began construction in Millard County in late 2025 and targets a 10 GW behind-the-meter AI data-center campus near Delta.
actions.access_caveat: Official state incentive page; it reports construction start and project claims but is not a building permit, energization, or completion record.

actions.result_status: County minutes show the Commission unanimously ratified a letter of support for the Creekstone Data Center Project. During the discussion, Commissioner Wright said established processes and legal requirements had been met, and described the project as having secured its own water rights and generating its own power.
actions.access_caveat: Support-letter ratification is supportive local-government evidence, not a new permit, building approval, or energization record.

actions.result_status: The staff report lists Creekstone Delta Gigasite Phase 1 at 220 MW UNDER CONST. and a 9,700+ MW expansion as PROPOSED. It also distinguishes public capacity scopes; no energization is stated.
actions.access_caveat: Government compiled inventory; approximate capacity and source limitations are stated in the report.
actions.evidence_note: Body/context retained from prior file: Grand County Planning Commission staff report / Utah public-notice system.

actions.result_status: Utah Public Notice agenda lists C-2 CUP application #Z-2026-043 for a major solar energy system approximately 6 miles southeast of Delta, with Creekstone Energy LLC as applicant. This is a solar/local-process item and not evidence that the data center is energized.
actions.access_caveat: Agenda notice only; July 9 minutes or final recommendation were not located in this refresh.
actions.evidence_note: Official public-notice record for related solar infrastructure.

actions.result_status: Creekstone announced 43,000 Dth/day of firm Kern River natural-gas transportation capacity for the Delta Gigasite, described as enough firm fuel to support roughly 220 MW of behind-the-meter generation for the first block of a campus master-planned above 10 GW.
actions.access_caveat: Company press release; underlying Kern River transactional report was not independently retrieved in this refresh.
actions.evidence_note: Company/owner source for initial gas supply and first-block generation capacity.

actions.result_status: County Commission agenda scheduled a public hearing and possible approval for Creekstone C-2 CUP application #Z-2026-043 for a major solar energy system south of Highway 50 and Harding Junction.
actions.access_caveat: Agenda only; posted minutes or an official approval record for the August 4 item were not located as of the 2026-08-11 refresh.
actions.evidence_note: Official public-notice record for related solar infrastructure.
